question: A student tries 20 values of k and reports the test RMSE of the best one. What is wrong?

answers.answer: k must always be 5
answers.feedback: There is no single correct k; it depends on the data.

answers.answer: The test set was used to make a choice, so the reported error is likely too optimistic
answers.feedback: Correct: choices belong on the validation set; the test set is used once.

answers.answer: Nothing — trying more values is always better
answers.feedback: Trying values is fine, but on the validation set.

answers.answer: RMSE can't be computed on a test set
answers.feedback: It can; the issue is using it for choosing.

question: Feature A has an SD of 400 and feature B has an SD of 0.05. Without scaling, what happens to the distance?

answers.answer: The distance can't be computed
answers.feedback: It can, it's just dominated by one feature.

answers.answer: It depends almost entirely on feature B
answers.feedback: B's differences are tiny, so they barely change the distance.

answers.answer: Both features count equally
answers.feedback: Only after converting to standard units.

answers.answer: It depends almost entirely on feature A
answers.feedback: Correct: differences in A are thousands of times larger.

question: What is the main difference between kNN classification and kNN regression?

answers.answer: Classification doesn't use distances
answers.feedback: Both use the same distances.

answers.answer: Classification only works with one feature
answers.feedback: It works with any number of features.

answers.answer: Classification takes a majority vote of the neighbors; regression averages them
answers.feedback: Correct: the neighbor search is identical, only the final step differs.

answers.answer: Regression needs a validation set but classification doesn't
answers.feedback: Both benefit from a validation set for choosing k.

question: Why might kNN predict pKa only modestly better than guessing the average?

answers.answer: kNN only works for boiling points
answers.feedback: kNN works for any numerical target.

answers.answer: pKa can't be predicted by any method
answers.feedback: Better models with more features do much better; see the Raddi & Voelz paper.

answers.answer: The five features capture only part of what controls acidity
answers.feedback: Correct: acidity depends on details of the structure that these few numbers may not capture.

answers.answer: The training set is too similar to the test set
answers.feedback: If anything, similarity would help.
